review_basis: Nine actual GitHub Actions Chromium PNGs were opened and semantically inspected at player height alongside their immutable player/contact metadata. No source/test/metric inferred a visual finding.
review_focus: Built-world plausibility, support logic, material family separation, dressing and distant layering.

frames.what_is_visible: A large cracked roof slab fills the foreground. Black parapet/step bands, thin oxide nosings, two flat brown side façades and the distant Kinetic Permit frame form a straight enclosed corridor.
what_looks_bad: The composition is heavy and low-value: the dark bands cut across the eye line while the destination is small and visually buried behind stacked rails.
The player sees textured slabs but not credible assemblies: walls are monolithic, equipment lacks connections and the lower harbour is hidden.
placeholder_signals: Simple cuboids, flat black rails, brown wall planes, uniformly spaced roof seams and a single small orange route stripe still read as assembled prototype modules.
repetition: The roof seam grooves and black/orange horizontal bands repeat on the same alignment, making the first approach read as a ladder of cloned bars.
unconvincing_elements: The side walls show no readable bays, service access, embedded openings or believable relationship to a lower operating harbour.
frames.dead_zone_assessment: The forward corridor has no open lateral vista or layered lower world. The blue sky is clean, but it is atmosphere above an enclosed set rather than depth through it.
missing: A clear lower rail/harbour glimpse, varied roof servicing, an adjacent occupied building face and a readable next landing beyond the permit.
replace: Replace the current black/oxide bar silhouette with fewer clearly supported circulation/structure elements where it blocks the player eye line.

strengths: The player-height view is no longer sky-only; roof surface, objective sign and immediate route direction are visible.
Frame metadata honestly marks authored support versus navigation misses.
defects: The player sees textured slabs but not credible assemblies: walls are monolithic, equipment lacks connections and the lower harbour is hidden.
Six of nine requested-region frames miss their requested destination; none may be treated as whole-run evidence.
The visible Dispatch/Switch imagery remains materially and structurally repetitive with no open lower-harbour vista.
